thread.title: Stock Market Hits New Highs As Big Techs, Marijuana Stocks On Fire

author: NANCY GONDO
title: Stock Market Hits New Highs As Big Techs, Marijuana Stocks On Fire
text:
Key market indexes opened mixed Wednesday but closed with solid gains as the Nasdaq composite and S&P 500 rallied to new highs in the stock market today .
X The Nasdaq rose 1%, the S&P 500 advanced 0.6% and the Dow Jones industrial average added 0.2%. Small caps took part, too, as the Russell 2000 gained 0.4%.
Big-cap techs led the upside. On the Dow, Apple ( AAPL ), Microsoft ( MSFT ) and Cisco Systems ( CSCO ) were among the biggest movers with gains north of 1% each. Apple extended its win streak to a six days and marked yet another new high.
Amazon.com ( AMZN ) rose more than 3% to a record high, boosted by a price-target hike. Morgan Stanley lifted its target to 2,500 from 1,850 and maintained an overweight rating. It cited strong growth in advertising, Amazon Web Services and other high-margin businesses.

The stock remains in a buy zone from a recent bounce off its 10-week moving average.
Solar, internet retail and software makers were among the day's top industry group leaders. But automakers, department store retailers and tobacco stocks lagged.
Pot Stocks Hit Fresh Highs Tilray ( TLRY ) soared 19% to a new all-time high in fast turnover. Shares have rallied nearly 80% since clearing a 34.20 buy point of an IPO base. The cannabis products maker said it's developing a global portfolio of brands and expects federal legalization in the U.S. sooner than most people think. On Tuesday, Tilray topped Q2 sales views with a 95% jump to $9.7 million.
Among other marijuana stocks , Cronos Group ( CRON ) vaulted 14% to a new high, while Canopy Growth ( CGC ) added 7%. The three stocks helped lift IBD's biotech industry group to a 1.4% gain.
On the downside, Tesla ( TSLA ) weighed on automakers as it gave up 2% to slide further below its 200-day line.
